purpose: One decision table for how a producer reads a receiver's answer to a reading batch. Both producers evaluate every case and must agree, so a rule can only be implemented one way in each.

outcomes.delivered: The batch is done. Do not retain it and do not retry it.
outcomes.retain: Retain the batch under its own identity and retry it. Same events, same order, same sequence.
outcomes.suspend: Stop exporting for this credential. The batch is not retried and its events count as refused, which is a different counter from declined.

cases.name: accepted_all_new
cases.why: The ordinary case. Every event was stored.

cases.name: accepted_mixed_new_and_held
cases.why: A retry after a lost acknowledgement. One event was already held; the new one was stored. Nothing is lost, so nothing is retried.

cases.name: duplicate_is_delivered_not_loss
cases.why: Every event was already held. The receiver holds them, so the batch is delivered. Reading this as loss is the defect v2 exists to remove.

cases.name: partial_declined_event_is_permanent
cases.why: A declined event is permanently refused. It is counted and discarded rather than retried, because the answer will not change and the rest of the batch is stored.

cases.name: counts_violate_invariant
cases.why: All three count members are present and do not sum to the batch size, so the answer confirms nothing. The receiver answered, so the batch is retained under the attempt bound.

cases.name: body_is_not_json
cases.why: A 2xx whose body cannot be parsed is a transport failure, not a delivery, and is not counted toward the attempt bound.

cases.name: body_omits_status
cases.why: No safe reading exists for a missing status. Without a status the contract defines, the body is not evidence the receiver answered, so the batch is retried without counting toward the attempt bound.

cases.name: body_omits_accepted_events
cases.why: No safe reading exists for a missing accepted_events either.

cases.name: tolerated_omits_rejected_events
cases.why: A receiver part-way through its migration. Absence is read as no events rejected, so the batch is delivered rather than retried forever. The body is not conformant and the producer says so.

cases.name: tolerated_omits_duplicate_events
cases.why: Absence is read as zero and the invariant must still hold on that reading. The present terms account for one of two events, so the unaccounted event is retained rather than assumed held.

cases.name: terminal_refusal_suspends
cases.why: Every recorded property holds: 403, JSON media type, the recorded detail, no authentication challenge.

cases.name: bare_403_does_not_suspend
cases.why: A proxy or WAF can answer 403 with no body. Suspension is irreversible for the process, so it needs positive evidence the endpoint itself refused.

cases.name: 403_wrong_detail_does_not_suspend
cases.why: A proxy answering JSON with some other detail satisfies every property but the one that identifies the receiver's own refusal.

cases.name: 403_with_auth_challenge_does_not_suspend
cases.why: An authentication challenge says the credential can be re-presented, which contradicts a terminal refusal of it.

cases.name: 401_is_retried
cases.why: A credential can be re-issued, so 401 is not terminal.

cases.name: 422_is_retried
cases.why: 422 describes the request rather than the credential. Retrying keeps a serialisation fault visible instead of silencing export on one.

cases.name: 415_is_retried
cases.why: Same reason as 422.

cases.name: 404_is_retried
cases.why: The contract records no terminal case for 404, so nothing may claim to know one.

cases.name: 410_is_retried
cases.why: The contract records no terminal case for 410 either.

cases.name: 500_is_retried
cases.why: A server fault is transient by assumption and never ends a producer.

cases.name: 503_is_retried
cases.why: The redeploy case. This is the answer that ended the Android payload's process.

cases.name: transport_failure_is_retried
cases.why: No answer at all. Connection refused, DNS failure, timeout.

cases.name: 204_with_no_body_is_retried
cases.why: A 2xx carrying no body cannot be read, and the contract requires a producer to read one. Delivery is not assumed from the status line alone.

cases.name: unknown_status_value
cases.why: A status outside the closed set has no safe reading and is not this contract's answer, so it neither delivers the batch nor counts toward abandoning it.

cases.name: accepted_events_not_an_integer
cases.why: A count that is not an integer cannot be summed, so the invariant is unevaluable and the answer unreadable.

cases.name: accepted_events_negative
cases.why: A negative count is not a number of events. Nothing in the contract makes it readable.

cases.name: rejected_events_not_a_list
cases.why: The member's shape is part of the contract. A producer that coerced this would be inventing a count.

cases.name: rejected_events_entry_without_event_id
cases.why: A declined event the producer cannot name is one it cannot discard deliberately, so the answer is unreadable.

cases.name: rejected_events_exceeds_batch
cases.why: More declined events than were sent fails the invariant, and a producer must not count declines it never sent.

cases.name: all_events_declined
cases.why: Every event permanently refused. The batch is done because retrying cannot change the answer, and every event is counted as declined rather than sent.

cases.name: terminal_refusal_detail_with_surrounding_whitespace
cases.why: The detail is matched after trimming, so a receiver's formatting does not decide whether a suspension is recognised.

cases.name: unmigrated_receiver_duplicate_with_nothing_stored
cases.why: What a receiver that has not migrated answers when it rejects a batch on `sequence`: a 200 saying nothing was stored, with neither of the members that would let a producer check. Reading this as delivered is the loss this version exists to remove, and the migration clause must not readmit it.

cases.name: tolerated_omission_that_accounts_for_the_batch
cases.why: The tolerance still applies where it is safe: rejected_events is absent, and the accepted count alone accounts for every event sent.

cases.name: declined_exceeds_batch_without_a_summable_invariant
cases.why: More events declined than were sent, in the shape where the invariant cannot catch it. A producer must not count declines it never sent: declined_events is what an operator reads as permanent loss, and it would become remote input.

cases.name: accepted_events_boolean
cases.why: `true` reads as 1 in one producer's JSON library and is not a number at all in the other's. Refused in both, so the two cannot disagree about it.

cases.name: accepted_events_non_integer
cases.why: A receiver written where 1 and 1.0 are the same number sends 1.0. Refused in both producers rather than accepted by one and retried forever by the other.

cases.name: duplicate_events_malformed
cases.why: The invariant has three terms and one of them was unguarded by this set. A present but unreadable duplicate count makes the answer unsummable, which is the shape that hid the original loss.

cases.name: count_wider_than_the_other_producer_can_hold
cases.why: An integer beyond u64 is unbounded in one producer and unrepresentable in the other. Refused in both.

cases.name: rejected_events_entry_with_an_empty_event_id
cases.why: A declined event the producer cannot name is one it cannot discard deliberately or log, and the decline counter would increment against nothing.

cases.name: refusal_under_a_json_suffix_media_type
cases.why: A structured suffix type is a JSON media type. Both branches of that test were uncovered, and a substring match on "json" would let a WAF error page suspend a device permanently.

cases.name: refusal_under_an_uppercased_media_type
cases.why: Media types are case-insensitive, so the comparison is made on a folded value.

cases.name: refusal_under_a_media_type_merely_containing_json
cases.why: `text/jsonish` is not a JSON media type. A substring match would accept it, and with it any intermediary body that reproduced the recorded detail.

cases.name: tolerated_omits_rejected_with_duplicates_present
cases.why: A per-event idempotent receiver that omits only rejected_events, answering a retry after a lost acknowledgement. The absent member is read as zero and the present ones account for the batch, so this is delivered. Requiring accepted plus declined alone would retain it forever.

cases.name: rejected_events_entry_not_an_object
cases.why: A declined event must be named by an object carrying event_id. A bare number names nothing.

cases.name: negative_count_whose_magnitude_would_sum
cases.why: The earlier negative case summed wrong even if a producer took the magnitude. This one sums correctly if it does, so a lenient reading of -1 as 1 is caught.

cases.name: count_that_would_wrap_an_unsigned_sum
cases.why: u64::MAX plus 2 is 1 in wrapping arithmetic. No count may exceed the batch size, which is what keeps the sum from wrapping in a release build, panicking in a debug one or truncating on a 32-bit phone.

cases.name: count_that_would_truncate_on_a_32_bit_phone
cases.why: 2^32 + 1 truncates to 1 as a 32-bit usize. It exceeds the batch size and is refused on every architecture.

cases.name: refusal_detail_with_a_separator_control_character
cases.why: Only ASCII space, tab, CR and LF are trimmed from the detail. Python's strip also removes U+001C, which Rust's trim keeps, so a trim left to either language suspends one producer and not the other.

cases.name: nan_in_an_unrelated_member
cases.why: NaN is not JSON. One parser accepts it and the other refuses the whole body, so both refuse it.

cases.name: refusal_carrying_infinity_in_another_member
cases.why: The recorded refusal plus a member no strict parser reads. It suspended one producer and not the other; it suspends neither.

cases.name: number_out_of_range
cases.why: 1e400 has no finite value. One parser reads infinity and the other refuses the body.

cases.name: escaped_lone_surrogate
cases.why: An escaped unpaired surrogate decodes to no Unicode scalar value.

cases.name: refusal_carrying_an_escaped_lone_surrogate
cases.why: The same, in a refusal body, where the disagreement was a suspension on one producer only.

cases.name: escaped_surrogate_pair_is_readable
cases.why: A correctly paired escape is one scalar value, and both producers read it.

cases.name: nesting_at_the_depth_bound
cases.why: 32 containers open at once, the root object counted as the first. Readable.

cases.name: nesting_beyond_the_depth_bound
cases.why: 33 containers. Refused by a scan before any parser runs, so neither a parser's recursion limit nor a RecursionError decides the answer.

cases.name: brackets_inside_a_string_do_not_nest
cases.why: Depth is counted outside strings.

cases.name: deep_nesting_within_the_size_ceiling
cases.why: 60 KB of nesting fits under the size ceiling and must not reach a recursive parser: in one producer it raised out of the flush loop and dropped a drained batch from every counter.

cases.name: byte_order_mark
cases.why: A byte-order mark before an otherwise conformant body. One decoder strips it and the other refuses it.

cases.name: utf16_encoded_body
cases.why: A conformant body encoded as UTF-16. One decoder detects the encoding and the other refuses it.

cases.name: refusal_encoded_as_utf16
cases.why: The recorded refusal as UTF-16. It suspended one producer's export for good; it suspends neither.

cases.name: invalid_utf8
cases.why: A raw lone surrogate byte sequence is not UTF-8.

cases.name: negative_zero_count
cases.why: -0 is not a count: a count is an unsigned integer token. One parser reads it as the integer 0 and the other as a floating-point number, so without a rule this body is delivered by one producer and retained by the other.

cases.name: integer_beyond_the_float_range
cases.why: An integer literal of 400 digits has no finite value as a 64-bit float. One parser holds it as an arbitrary-precision integer and the other refuses the body, so both refuse it.

cases.name: integer_beyond_u64_within_the_float_range
cases.why: An integer of 30 digits exceeds every fixed-width integer and is still a finite float, so the body is readable in both producers.

cases.name: integer_just_inside_the_float_range
cases.why: 179 followed by 306 zeros rounds to the largest finite 64-bit float.

cases.name: integer_just_beyond_the_float_range
cases.why: 18 followed by 307 zeros rounds to infinity.

cases.name: repeated_count_member
cases.why: accepted_events named twice. Which occurrence a parser keeps is the library's choice, so a producer that kept the last would deliver this and one that kept the first would retain it. The body is unreadable.

cases.name: repeated_member_spelled_with_an_escape
cases.why: The same name, once written with an escape. Names are compared after decoding, so this is a repetition.

cases.name: repeated_member_in_a_nested_object
cases.why: A repetition anywhere makes the body unreadable, not only among the members a producer reads.

cases.name: repeated_detail_in_a_refusal
cases.why: Kept last, this is the recorded refusal and suspends export for good; kept first, it is not. It suspends neither.

cases.name: escaped_member_name
cases.why: A member name written with an escape decodes to the name it spells, and is read as that member.

cases.name: number_that_underflows
cases.why: 1e-400 rounds to zero, which is finite. Readable in both producers.

cases.name: a_portals_json_object_is_not_the_receiver_answering
cases.why: A captive portal answering 200 with a JSON object of its own. It confirms nothing, and it is not evidence the receiver declined to confirm, so it must not count toward discarding the batch.

cases.name: a_contract_shaped_answer_under_another_media_type_does_not_count
cases.why: A defined status that does not account for the batch, served as a web page. Retained, and not counted toward abandonment: discarding readings needs the receiver's own answer.

cases.name: a_confirming_answer_under_another_media_type_still_delivers
cases.why: Counts that account for every event confirm the batch whatever the media type claims.

cases.name: rejected_events_naming_one_event_twice
cases.why: Two declined entries for one event account for a two-event batch only by counting the same event twice.

cases.name: tolerated_omits_only_duplicate_events
cases.why: duplicate_events absent, read as zero, and the rest accounts for the batch. Delivered, and reported as non-conformant: that report is the only sign a receiver has not migrated.

cases.name: escaped_quote_before_nesting_beyond_the_bound
cases.why: An escaped quote inside a string must not end the string for the depth scan, or the nesting after it is not counted.

cases.name: escaped_quote_before_nesting_at_the_bound
cases.why: The same escape with nesting at the bound. Readable.

cases.name: closing_bracket_before_any_opening
cases.why: Malformed, and the depth scan must not underflow on it: in a debug build that is a panic that ends the process.

cases.name: lone_surrogate_as_a_member_name
cases.why: An escaped unpaired surrogate in a member name decodes to no Unicode scalar value, as it does in a string value.

cases.name: refusal_detail_with_a_trailing_vertical_tab
cases.why: Vertical tab is not among the trimmed characters, though one language's notion of whitespace includes it.

cases.name: refusal_detail_wrapped_in_crlf
cases.why: Carriage return and line feed are trimmed from both ends, so this is the recorded refusal.

cases.name: largest_double_written_as_an_exact_integer
cases.why: The exact integer value of the largest double is finite. A parser that rounds approximately near the top of the range refuses it, so both producers round correctly.

cases.name: integer_one_below_the_rounding_halfway_point
cases.why: One below the point halfway between the largest double and the next power of two rounds down to the largest double.

cases.name: integer_at_the_rounding_halfway_point
cases.why: Exactly halfway rounds to even, which is infinity.

cases.name: largest_double_in_shortest_decimal_form
cases.why: 1.7976931348623158e308 rounds to the largest double.

cases.name: refusal_carrying_the_largest_double
cases.why: The recorded refusal with a finite number at the top of the range. It suspended one producer and not the other; it suspends both.

cases.name: refusal_under_two_media_types
cases.why: Content-Type sent twice, JSON first. Joined, the media type is not JSON, so this is not the recorded refusal for either producer, whichever value its client would have kept.

cases.name: refusal_under_two_media_types_reversed
cases.why: The same, with JSON second.

cases.name: gzip_coded_success
cases.why: A producer requests no content coding and decodes none. A coded body is unreadable, whatever it decodes to.

cases.name: deflate_coded_refusal
cases.why: The recorded refusal under a content coding. Unreadable, so not a refusal.

cases.name: identity_coding_is_readable
cases.why: identity is no coding, in any case and with surrounding space.

cases.name: identity_then_gzip
cases.why: Content-Encoding sent twice. Joined, it names a coding, so the body is unreadable.

cases.name: empty_content_encoding_is_readable
cases.why: An empty Content-Encoding names no coding.

cases.name: x_gzip_coding_is_unreadable
cases.why: x-gzip is a coding by another name.

cases.name: refusal_under_an_empty_challenge_then_a_real_one
cases.why: WWW-Authenticate sent twice, the first empty. Joined, there is a challenge, so this is not the refusal.

cases.name: refusal_with_a_challenge_carrying_a_non_ascii_byte
cases.why: A challenge whose realm holds bytes outside visible ASCII, in a field the verdict reads. Clients decode such bytes differently, so the answer is no answer, and in particular not a suspension.

cases.name: success_with_a_control_byte_in_an_unrelated_header
cases.why: A control byte in a field the verdict does not read. The parser accepts it, and nothing the verdict depends on can be decoded differently, so the answer is read.

cases.name: success_with_utf8_in_an_unrelated_header
cases.why: A site name in UTF-8 on an unrelated field is not a reason to hold readings for good.

cases.name: refusal_under_a_transfer_coding_other_than_chunked
cases.why: Transfer-Encoding gzip, chunked. Only a single chunked coding is read; anything else is no answer.

cases.name: chunked_in_any_case_is_readable
cases.why: chunked is case-insensitive.

cases.name: transfer_encoding_sent_twice
cases.why: Two Transfer-Encoding fields, even both chunked, are no answer.

cases.name: refusal_with_conflicting_content_lengths
cases.why: Two different lengths are no answer; neither is chosen.

cases.name: content_length_sent_twice_with_one_value
cases.why: Identical lengths are one length.

cases.name: content_length_listing_one_value_twice
cases.why: A comma-separated list of one repeated value is that value.

cases.name: content_length_with_twenty_digits
cases.why: Leading zeros up to twenty digits are a decimal length.

cases.name: content_length_with_twenty_one_digits
cases.why: More than twenty digits is no answer.

cases.name: content_length_and_transfer_encoding_together
cases.why: Both framings at once is the shape of a smuggled response, and no producer reads it.

cases.name: a_single_content_length_is_readable
cases.why: The ordinary case.

cases.name: a_body_of_exactly_the_ceiling_is_read
cases.why: A conformant answer padded with whitespace to exactly 64 KiB, declared as such.

cases.name: a_body_declared_one_byte_past_the_ceiling_is_not_read
cases.why: Declared past the ceiling, so refused before a byte of it is read.

cases.name: a_close_delimited_body_past_the_ceiling_is_not_read
cases.why: No length and no coding: read until close, and stopped past the ceiling. The first 64 KiB alone would confirm.

cases.name: a_close_delimited_body_is_read
cases.why: No length and no coding: the body runs to the end of the connection.

cases.name: a_header_line_without_a_colon
cases.why: A line that is not a field. One client panicked on it and ended the process; it is no answer.

cases.name: a_refusal_carrying_a_line_without_a_colon
cases.why: The recorded refusal with a line that is not a field. No answer, so not a suspension.

cases.name: a_refusal_with_a_space_before_the_colon
cases.why: WWW-Authenticate followed by a space is not a field name. Dropped by one client, it left a refusal with no challenge.

cases.name: a_refusal_with_an_empty_field_name
cases.why: A line beginning with a colon is not a field.

cases.name: a_folded_content_encoding
cases.why: Content-Encoding: identity continued on a folded line by gzip reads as the single value `identity gzip`, which names a coding.

cases.name: a_refusal_with_a_folded_challenge
cases.why: A challenge on a folded line is still a challenge.

cases.name: a_folded_line_before_any_field
cases.why: A continuation with nothing to continue is no answer.

cases.name: a_refusal_after_100_continue
cases.why: Interim responses are read past. The final answer is the recorded refusal.

cases.name: a_confirmation_after_103_early_hints
cases.why: Early Hints from a CDN precede the receiver's answer. Read as the final answer, it stopped export for good.

cases.name: switching_protocols_is_not_an_answer_to_a_batch
cases.why: 101 ends the exchange with the protocol switched; nothing confirms the batch.

cases.name: http_1_0_refusal_marked_chunked_but_not_chunked
cases.why: A transfer coding frames the body whatever the version, and this body is not chunked: no answer.

cases.name: http_1_0_confirmation_genuinely_chunked
cases.why: The same framing, genuinely chunked, is read.

cases.name: a_chunked_trailer_with_an_illegal_line
cases.why: The trailer section is read with the same field rules as the header section.

cases.name: bare_line_feeds_are_line_ends
cases.why: A response whose lines end in LF alone is read.

cases.name: a_leading_blank_line_is_no_response_line
cases.why: A blank line where the status line belongs is no answer.

cases.name: a_status_line_without_a_reason
cases.why: The reason phrase is optional.

cases.name: a_tab_inside_the_media_type
cases.why: A tab is whitespace a field value may hold, and the media type before the parameter is still JSON.

cases.name: a_body_cut_short_of_its_length
cases.why: A body that ends before its declared length is no answer.

cases.name: a_folded_unrelated_header_is_read
cases.why: A folded line continues the field before it; it does not make the response malformed.

cases.name: refusal_with_a_header_section_past_the_field_limit
cases.why: More than 100 KiB of field names and values. One parser refuses such a section only while it is incomplete, which depends on how the bytes arrived; measured on the parsed fields, it is no answer for every producer.

cases.name: confirmation_with_a_large_header_section_within_the_limit
cases.why: A header section under the limit is read.

cases.name: refusal_under_a_non_ascii_media_type_parameter
cases.why: A byte outside visible ASCII in Content-Type, a field the verdict reads. No answer, and so not a suspension.

cases.name: content_lengths_that_differ_only_by_a_leading_zero
cases.why: Repeated lengths are compared as written, not as numbers: 83 and 083 conflict.

counters.declined_events: Events a receiver reported in rejected_events. Permanently refused, counted, discarded.
counters.refused_events: Events discarded because a terminal refusal suspended export.
counters.receiver_answered: Whether the receiver's application answered: a 2xx over a JSON media type whose readable object carries a status this contract defines. A batch that keeps receiving such an answer without confirmation is abandoned after a bounded number of attempts; any other retained batch is retried for as long as memory allows.
counters.duplicate_events: Events the receiver reported it already held. Delivered, and counted apart.
counters.body_unreadable: Whether an answer arrived whose body could not be read, as distinct from no answer at all.

body_encodings.body: a JSON value, serialised as compact UTF-8
body_encodings.body_raw: text, encoded as UTF-8 byte for byte; for bodies no JSON value can express
body_encodings.body_b64: exact bytes, base64; for a byte-order mark, UTF-16, or invalid UTF-8
body_encodings.headers: content_type, www_authenticate and content_encoding may be a list: the header was sent that many times, and its values are joined with ", " in order before the rule reads them.
body_encodings.raw_response_b64: A whole HTTP/1.1 response, base64, read by each producer's own HTTP parser. A response its parser refuses is no answer at all.
